details:
1. Install the drivers for the 3dconnexion SpaceMouse

2. Launch VRChat (in desktop *or* VR!)

3. Open anything that scrolls vertically (i.e. the settings screen, the worlds list)

4. Try scrolling it in the usual way

5. You can move it fine, but then as soon as you stop dragging it, it automatically scrolls back up to the top too quickly for you to use anything beyond the first screen

I'd like to point out that this problem happens *even if the SpaceMouse is NOT PLUGGED IN; just having the drivers installed seems to cause the problem.

There's a thread on their forums here https://forum.3dconnexion.com/viewtopic.php?p=111133 that describes the apparent solution on VRChat's side of things:

"These are probably using the old Input Manager. You may need to change the "Get Motion from all Joysticks" option on some (all) Axes definitions.

I didn't find a disable/remove.

Possibly Mouse ScrollWheel is enough. I remapped all of them."

It also describes a workaround for SpaceMouse users, although it requires disabling part of their drivers, which prevents using the SpaceMouse as a gamepad substitute deliberately in other applications....   I'll record those instructions here for posterity at least, since their forum isn't accessible on the Wayback machine, and I know I'm not the only VRChat user dealing with this:

- Open the Device Manager

- Open Human Interface Devices

- go through all the entries named "HID-compliant game controller", and on each one:

-- right-click and select Properties

-- click the Details tab

-- in the Property dropdown, select Device instance path

-- see if the Value field starts with "HID\3DXKMJ_HIDMINI&COL03..."

-- if so, click the Driver tab and then click Disable Device

though as mentioned, bear in mind that this will apparently prevent you from mapping SpaceMouse inputs to gamepad inputs in other games (though applications with the native API, like the Unity Editor, still function)
title: 3dconnexion SpaceMouse drivers prevent scrolling interface
